A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TimeBridge and contain the main paper and Appendices A–G. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, tables and figures despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original TimeBridge forecasting results, architectural ablations, attention analyses and financial portfolio evaluations in Sections 4–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original forecasting, financial and ablation results, revises some outcomes, and adds empirical results on the Climate dataset.

M1.justification: The patch embedding, Integrated Attention, patch downsampling and Cointegrated Attention procedures remain unchanged. v3 newly documents a hybrid training loss, but v1 specifies no loss, so the PDFs do not establish an actual objective change. Dataset-specific configuration revisions are assessed under E3.

E1.justification: v3 adds Climate, comprising regional precipitation measurements from 1,763 Australian stations, to long-term forecasting evaluation. This extends geographic and high-dimensional data coverage within the existing forecasting task; all earlier datasets and tasks remain.

E2.justification: DeformableTST replaces PDF in the long-term numerical comparisons and statistical comparison: v1 Tables 2, 11 and 17 correspond to v3 Tables 1, 9 and 15. TSMixer is added to both financial comparison tables in v3, having been absent from v1 Tables 4 and 12. Other corresponding comparator memberships are retained.

E3.justification: v3 removes the separate comparison using baseline papers’ original results, retaining the hyperparameter-search protocol. Reported configurations also change substantially: ETTh2 and ETTm1 patch counts fall from 30 to 12 and 15, respectively; several ETT widths and learning rates change; and Electricity changes from two Integrated/one Cointegrated layers to one/two. Climate receives its own split and configuration. These are reported setting revisions, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The normalization, attention-order, CI/CD and downsampling studies retain their questions and variant sets, but their reference TimeBridge results are revised for Weather and Electricity. These are limited updates to existing analyses in v1 Tables 13–16 and v3 Tables 11–14, rather than newly introduced ablation studies.

E5.justification: Both Appendix F sections state that experiments are repeated three times and report standard deviations alongside the same 99% and 95% confidence-label format. Replacing the long-term comparator and adding Climate extend the existing reporting practice without changing the disclosed uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: The long-term result set is substantially revised, with original-setting results removed and Climate and DeformableTST results added. Between v1 Table 2 and v3 Table 1, TimeBridge’s ETTm1 MSE/MAE changes from 0.353/0.388 to 0.344/0.379, and Weather from 0.218/0.259 to 0.219/0.249. TimeMixer’s Electricity result changes from 0.156/0.246 to 0.185/0.284. Configuration revisions prevent interpreting these as controlled performance gains. PeMS and existing financial results are retained, with TSMixer financial results added.

T1.justification: Appendix D newly defines the weighted time-domain and FFT-domain MAE objective, L = (1−alpha)Lt + alpha Lf. This is a limited addition of a mathematical definition. The integration, cointegration and ADF/EG mathematics in Appendix A remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: remove non-stationarity for short-term temporal modeling, preserve it for long-term cross-variate relationships, and achieve strong forecasting and financial performance. Added benchmark evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 Appendix D adds the rationale that MAE stabilizes optimization relative to MSE and that frequency-domain supervision mitigates label autocorrelation. The Climate discussion also interprets performance in terms of high dimensionality, noise and inter-channel dependencies. Earlier interpretations and the qualification about weak cointegration in ETT remain.

D1.justification: v3 discloses the previously unspecified hybrid loss, its FreDF attribution and dataset-specific mixing weights in Appendix D and Table 8. It also supplies Climate configuration details and revises existing hyperparameter entries. The code-access statement, hardware, batch-size policy and ten-epoch training budget remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to DeformableTST, TSMixer, the Monash forecasting archive and FreDF, while removing Lai et al. (2018) and Li et al. (2024). These update experimental and implementation context; the broader positioning around normalization and channel-independent versus channel-dependent modeling remains stable.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the experimental discussion, an expanded implementation appendix, a new Impact Statement and correction of the author name Tai Dai to Tao Dai. Most prose and the main section and appendix sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, with widespread resizing and relocation of figures and tables. Figure 1 is condensed from four paired groups into two forecast plots. The original-results tables disappear, while retained tables gain Climate or TSMixer entries and an alpha column; appendix visualizations are redistributed across pages.

improvement.justification: Specifying the previously undocumented loss and its mixing weights addresses a reproducibility omission, while Climate and additional comparator results modestly strengthen the evidence. These gains are limited by narrower long-term comparisons and new inconsistencies between Section 4’s fixed patch count/learning-rate list and Table 8. The net improvement is limited; revised scores under changed configurations do not independently establish better scientific quality.
